Hi @SYN-bit , 

The file [sip-rtp-opus-hybird.pcap](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/uploads/b94fd091a3c2b0563487da61e189cf1e/sip-rtp-opus-hybird.pcap) include 5 different opus example frames.

Thanks

Hi, @sun.lin, how did you get that capture? [RFC 6716](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6716.html#section-3.2.5) is very clear that the Opus padding occurs at the end of the packet, not immediately after the padding length bytes, and must be all zero.

The patch dissects them immediately after the padding length bytes; interpreting your sample capture according to the specification makes it malformed - and indeed, the Opus reference decoder rejects the packets.

Hi @johnthacker 
I remember I created the pcap file from one empty packet, clone the packet and modified the header fields for different scenarios and assemble the modified packets into one pcap file. That's why the one pcap file contains variants packets. 
And the packets only for dissects demo only. They were filled by me, didn't contains real opus data.
There is no simple way to construct variants opus packets in one pcap file.

Thanks. I noticed that the Opus decoder library rejected the packets with padding as malformed (but was fine with the ones with two frames in a packet), and wanted to check. The dissector should probably be fixed as well.

A more difficult project is eventually handling stereo properly.

When I got spare time, I'll try to refill the `ip-rtp-opus-hybird.pcap` with valid opus packets.
Or anyone who can fix this sample pcap file with valid opus data are welcome.
